children.name: Section label
children.characters: COREDESK / PRODUCT PLANNING / 10 SEPTEMBER 2026

children.name: Board title
children.characters: Make the work clear before making the screens.

children.name: Summary
children.characters: Proposed product scope • Planning artifacts only • No new application UI

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
Product promise
A focused workspace for independent professionals to manage a client relationship, run a project, write its documents, collect a decision and deliver the right version.

Primary user and V1 assumption
One workspace owner runs a freelance business. External clients enter a small, invite-only review experience. Internal team seats and multi-workspace management follow V1.

First complete journey
Enter → create client → define project → plan tasks → draft document → request review → revise → approve → deliver → retrieve history.

Three different records
CLIENT = the ongoing relationship.
PROJECT = one scoped engagement with an outcome.
DOCUMENT = a versioned piece of work.
Tasks, milestones, reviews and delivery packages link to these records.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
V1 success
The owner always knows the next action, where work belongs, which version the client saw, what was decided and what was delivered.

Product boundaries
Core: client work, projects, tasks and documents.
Guest review: a narrow extension of Core.
Later sub-applications: Portfolio, Finance, Developer.
Later Core capabilities: team seats, integrations, advanced AI and automations.

How to read this file
01  Brief and research: why these decisions.
02  Feature map and IA: objects and navigation.
03  Page inventory: content, actions and states.
04  Lifecycles and access: behavior and rules.
05  Roadmap and validation: order and release gates.

Status of decisions
The release boundaries are a proposed baseline, not a claim that features already exist. Original Foundations, palette, logo and gradient references are retained.

children.name: Section label
children.characters: RESEARCH / BRAND & INTERACTION

children.name: Board title
children.characters: Borrow principles. Keep CoreDesk’s identity.

children.name: Summary
children.characters: Fresh source review on 10 September 2026. Historical awards are references, not claims of current rankings.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
R1 · Dala / Awwwards
Evidence: a workplace-information product presented alongside reactive-cursor and WebGL highlights.
Apply: articulate the utility before visual spectacle; make search return work with its client/project context.
Avoid: translating showcase motion into repeated workspace actions.
Source: https://www.awwwards.com/sites/dala

R2 · Noomo / Awwwards case study
Evidence: the studio describes brand-derived motifs, navigation testing and performance fixes.
Apply: derive future visual rules from the retained CoreDesk logo and palette; test unfamiliar navigation.
Avoid: borrowing the studio’s motifs or copying its website structure.
Source: https://www.awwwards.com/new-focus-new-brand-new-website.html

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
R3 · Contra / Project Cost Calculator
Evidence: the live tool takes scoped inputs, presents a breakdown and supports reset/retry. Its studio lists the project on Awwwards.
Apply: guide project creation, then show an editable summary; explain calculated values and recovery paths.
Avoid: the 3D presentation and its rate assumptions.
Sources:
https://contra.com/project-rate-hiring-calculator/
https://www.awwwards.com/unseenstudio/?library=true&previewmode=true

Direction for later UI work
Authentication should make the brand recognizable while keeping sign-in, legal links and recovery clear.
Working pages need clear hierarchy, calm density and consistent context. Documents deserve a real writing and preview surface.
Gradients and motion remain future composition decisions.

Research limits
This is public-page and official-documentation research. Awwwards is visual/interaction inspiration, not proof of authenticated app usability. No competitor layout or screenshot was copied.

children.name: Section label
children.characters: RESEARCH / WORKFLOW & CONTENT

children.name: Board title
children.characters: Useful patterns become product requirements.

children.name: Summary
children.characters: Evidence is summarized below. CoreDesk recommendations are our synthesis, not descriptions of competitor features.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
R4 · Linear / Concepts & Project Overview
Evidence: projects, tasks, milestones and views have distinct roles; an overview holds purpose and resources.
Apply: keep one task record across all views. Project Overview contains scope, owner, dates, milestones, references and next action.
https://linear.app/docs/conceptual-model
https://linear.app/docs/project-overview

R5 · Notion / Projects and tasks
Evidence: linked projects/tasks and contextual views keep related work together.
Apply: client and project context remain available while writing. Supply defaults; avoid requiring users to build a database system first.
https://www.notion.com/help/guides/getting-started-with-projects-and-tasks

R6 · HoneyBook / Pipeline
Evidence: engagement stages and configured event-driven movement are separate.
Apply: use clear manual project stages in V1; keep overdue and waiting as attention flags.
https://help.honeybook.com/en/articles/2463528-customize-your-pipeline-in-honeybook

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
R7 · Bonsai / Client Portal
Evidence: central client actions, visibility settings and client preview.
Apply: guest pages expose assigned reviews and delivery only; the owner previews exactly what will be shared.
https://help.hellobonsai.com/en/articles/4409019-how-to-use-the-client-portal

R8 · Basecamp / Client visibility
Evidence: internal content and explicitly client-visible content are distinguished.
Apply: private by default; internal notes never become client-visible when a document is shared.
https://5.basecamp-help.com/article/1082-what-clients-can-see-and-do

R9 · HoneyBook / Previous file versions
Evidence: editable drafts and previously shared file versions are distinct.
Apply: freeze submitted versions and bind each decision to one version.
https://help.honeybook.com/en/articles/6804807-view-a-previous-version-of-your-file

Concrete output
Consistent client metadata; context-preserving project views; explicit draft/review/delivery states; recovery and access states in every page contract.

children.name: Board title
children.characters: One Core. Specialist applications later.

children.name: Summary
children.characters: Read each branch as a capability group. V1 includes a complete owner-to-client delivery loop.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
COREDESK → CORE [V1]
├─ Enter & orient
│   Auth entry, sign in/up, recovery, onboarding
│   Home queue, search, activity
├─ Manage relationships
│   Clients, contacts, next action, private notes
│   Active/past projects and relationship history
├─ Run engagements
│   Scope, milestones, tasks, documents, files
│   Review progress, delivery and archive
└─ Create documents
    Brief, proposal, agreement record, welcome pack
    Notes and deliverable documents
    Structured editor, fixed templates, PDF export
    Working draft, submitted versions and history

CORE → GUEST REVIEW [V1]
Verified invite → shared project → assigned version
→ comment / request changes / approve → download
One designated approver per review request.
This is a restricted Core experience, not a full CRM.

SHARED CORE SERVICES [V1]
Identity • canonical records • search • save state
Activity • scoped access • archive/restore
In-app notifications and transactional access email

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
CORE EXTENSIONS [V1.1 / LATER]
Internal seats and roles; multiple reviewers.
Reusable custom templates; import/export improvements.
Email/calendar connections; reminders and automations.
Optional AI drafting with review and source context.
Local/cloud AI controls arrive with AI, not before.

PORTFOLIO [V2 / OPTIONAL SUB-APP]
Case studies → media → consent → preview → publish.
Reuses delivered project material by explicit selection.
No automatic client-content publication.

FINANCE [V2 / OPTIONAL SUB-APP]
Estimates → invoices → payments → expenses/reports.
Native e-signature is a later integration/capability.
V1 may store proposed fees; it does not collect money.

DEVELOPER [V3 / SEPARATE DISCOVERY]
Overview → Code → CLI → Agents.
Own workbench, files, terminals, runs and approvals.
Shares identity and optional project links.
No IDE, terminal or agent execution in V1.

SCOPE RULE
A new feature must help the V1 delivery loop or be assigned to a later branch. No inactive future-app links in the V1 navigation.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
Public entry
Auth Entry [A01]
→ Sign In [A02] / Sign Up [A03]
→ Verify [A04] / Recover access [A05]
→ Onboarding [A06] → Home [W01]
Terms & Privacy [A07–08] remain publicly reachable.

Owner workspace / persistent navigation
HOME [W01]              /home
CLIENTS [C01]           /clients
  Client Detail [C02]   /clients/:client
PROJECTS [P01]          /projects
  Project Workspace    /projects/:project
    Overview [P02] · Work [P03]
    Documents & Files [P04]
    Reviews [P05] · Delivery [P06]
TASKS [W02]             /tasks
DOCUMENTS [D01]         /documents
  Document Workspace [D02] /documents/:document
  Preview & History [D03–04] are document views.
ACTIVITY [W04]          /activity
SETTINGS [S01–03]       /settings/*
ARCHIVE [W05]           /archive
Search [W03] is one global overlay.

Context rules
Breadcrumb: Client → Project → Document.
Back returns to prior view/filter/selection.
Project tabs share one context header.
Client tabs are sections of C02, not duplicate apps.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
Guest / separate access surface
Invite & Verify [G01]    /review-access/:invite
Shared Project [G02]    /shared/:project
Review Version [G03]    /review/:request
Delivery [G04]          /delivery/:package
Guests never inherit the owner navigation.

Record model
Workspace 1 → many Clients
Client 1 → many Contacts + Projects
Project 1 → many Tasks + Milestones + Documents
Document 1 → many immutable Versions
Version 1 → many Review Requests over time
Review Request → one designated approver
Delivery Package → exact approved Versions/files
Access Grant → recipient + object + allowed actions

Single source of truth
Tasks and Documents are global views of project-owned records. Creating from a global view requires selecting a project. Client-level notes live in C02.
A document belongs to one project in V1.
A reference link does not duplicate ownership.
Client Kit is a filtered document set, not a new entity.

Future app navigation
An app switcher appears only when a second app ships.
Portfolio, Finance and Developer reuse IDs and access boundaries; they do not fork client/project data.

children.name: Board title

children.name: Summary
children.characters: Each entry specifies purpose, required content, actions and essential states. These are page contracts, not wireframes.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
A01 · Auth Entry [public page]
Contains: CoreDesk identity, short promise, Sign in, Create account, Terms and Privacy.
Actions: choose entry path.
States: loading, service unavailable, already signed in.
Later: Google SSO; show it only once implemented.

A02 · Sign In [public page]
Contains: email, password, recovery link, sign-up link.
Actions: sign in; retain intended destination.
States: invalid credentials, verification needed, rate limit, network failure, expired session.

A03 · Sign Up [public page]
Contains: name, email, password requirements, Terms/Privacy acknowledgment.
Actions: create account; go to verification.
States: existing email, weak password, validation and submission failure.

A04 · Verify Email [public page/state]
Contains: masked address, instructions, resend cooldown.
Actions: verify, resend, correct email.
States: pending, success, expired/used link, retry.
Success: resume onboarding or intended destination.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
A05 · Recover Access [two-step flow]
Contains: email request; new password and confirmation.
Actions: request reset; save new password.
States: generic request receipt, invalid/expired token, password mismatch, success, network retry.

A06 · Onboarding [workspace flow]
Contains: owner name, workspace name, timezone, optional brand/service defaults; first-client step.
Actions: save workspace; create first client or skip optional setup.
States: progress saved, resume, validation, failure.
Exit: Home shows an actionable first-work prompt.

A07 · Terms [public page]
Contains: version/effective date, owner-supplied terms, contact route, return link.
Actions: read and return.
States: content unavailable with recovery route.
Release dependency: actual approved copy, not placeholder legal claims.

A08 · Privacy [public page]
Contains: version/date, owner-supplied privacy copy, contact/data-request route.
Actions: read and return.
States: unavailable and return.
Both legal pages are linked from auth and settings.

children.name: Section label
children.characters: PAGE INVENTORY / 2 OF 6 / ALL V1

children.name: Board title
children.characters: The owner’s daily workspace

children.name: Summary
children.characters: Home, search, tasks and activity expose the same work records with different purposes.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
W01 · Home [page]
Contains: due/overdue work, awaiting client, new decisions, next actions and recently opened records; each item names its client/project.
Actions: resume work, open item, create client/project.
States: first run, all clear, loading, partial failure.
No decorative KPI requirement.

W02 · Tasks [page + detail panel]
Contains: title, project/client, due date, status, priority, milestone, owner; Today/Upcoming/Waiting/Done filters.
Detail: description, checklist, links and activity.
Actions: add, edit, complete, postpone, open project.
States: empty/filter-empty, overdue, blocked, save failure.
V1 statuses: To do → In progress → Done; Cancelled.

W03 · Search [global overlay]
Contains: query, grouped client/project/document/task results, context and recent items.
Actions: keyboard selection, open, clear, close.
States: no query, searching, no results, failure.
Only authorized records appear; archive is opt-in.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
W04 · Activity [page]
Contains: review requests, feedback, approval and delivery events; unread/all filters; actor, time and linked record.
Actions: open source, mark read, filter.
States: empty, deleted/unavailable target, retry.
Reading an event does not resolve its work item.

W05 · Archive [page]
Contains: clients/projects/documents, archive date, prior context and search.
Actions: inspect history, restore, filter.
States: empty, missing parent, restore conflict.
Archived records are read-only. Access revocation is separate.

C01 · Clients [page]
Contains per card/row: client name, relationship state, primary contact, active project count, next action and last activity.
Actions: add client, search/filter, open.
States: no clients, filter-empty, duplicate warning.
Card order and field placement stay consistent.

C02 · Client Detail [page with sections]
Contains: profile/contacts; active and past projects; document set; private notes; relationship history; next action.
Actions: edit contact, add project, open documents, change state, archive/restore.
States: prospect/no projects, inactive, archived.
No single linear project stage stands in for the whole relationship.

children.name: Preview status

children.name: Section label
children.characters: PAGE INVENTORY / 3 OF 6 / ALL V1

children.name: Board title
children.characters: Projects have a purpose and a delivery path.

children.name: Summary
children.characters: P02–P06 are tabs/views of one Project Workspace. Keep its identity and context visible throughout.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
P01 · Projects [page + create flow]
Contains: name, client, outcome, stage, due date, next milestone, next action and review progress.
Create: select client → brief/scope → dates → summary.
Actions: create, filter, sort, open.
States: empty, incomplete draft, overdue, on hold.
Reuse C02’s client when creating in context.

P02 · Project Overview [workspace tab]
Contains: brief, scope/out-of-scope, owner, client, dates, stage, milestones, key links/documents, next action and recent history.
Actions: edit scope/dates, record scope acceptance, change stage or place on hold.
States: draft/planned, active, blocked, cancelled, closed.
Scope changes after acceptance are recorded.

P03 · Project Work [workspace tab]
Contains: project tasks, milestone grouping, due dates, status and a readable progress count.
Actions: add/reorder tasks, edit milestone, complete task.
States: no tasks, completed, overdue, on hold.
Uses the same task detail panel as W02.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
P04 · Documents & Files [workspace tab]
Contains: title, type, latest draft/submitted version, review state, visibility, modified date; file name/size.
Actions: create document, upload file, attach link, open.
States: empty, upload progress/failure, unsupported file, unavailable link.
Project files are private until explicitly shared.

P05 · Reviews [workspace tab]
Contains: requested version, designated reviewer, due date, outcome, comments and pending action.
Actions: request review, open feedback, withdraw request, create revision.
States: none pending, waiting, overdue, changes requested, approved, superseded.
V1: one open request per deliverable.

P06 · Delivery [workspace tab]
Contains: exact approved versions/files, package title, recipient, handoff notes, delivery date and acknowledgment status.
Actions: preview as client, share package, copy link, record external handoff, close project.
States: missing approval/file, ready, delivered, access revoked.
Record acknowledgment separately from delivery.

Navigation consistency
Every tab can open its source document/task.
Review and delivery never create parallel copies.
Project closure does not archive its client.

children.name: Section label
children.characters: PAGE INVENTORY / 4 OF 6 / ALL V1

children.name: Board title
children.characters: A document is more than an editor.

children.name: Summary
children.characters: Proposal, brief, agreement record, welcome pack and deliverable share one document system.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
D01 · Documents [global page]
Contains: title/type, client/project, working and submitted version, review state, visibility, reviewer and due date.
Actions: filter/search, open, create in project.
States: empty, filter-empty, archived, load failure.

D02 · Document Workspace [page]
Contains: title/type, client/project, section outline, body, save status, current version, internal notes and separate client feedback.
Actions: edit, reorder sections, save, preview, submit, revise, export.
States: unsaved/saving/saved, failed save, conflicting edit, read-only shared version, missing assets.
V1 blocks: text, headings, lists, image and simple table.

D03 · Preview & Export [document view]
Contains: paginated preview, title/version, brand/template choice and export status.
Actions: return to edit, export PDF, open review setup.
States: overflow/content issue, rendering, export failure, success.
PDF identifies its version; preview never counts as sharing.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
D04 · Version History [document panel/view]
Contains: numbered submitted versions, author/date, decision status and delivery references.
Actions: inspect old version; copy to a new draft.
States: no submitted version, current, superseded.
Never overwrite a submitted version.

D05 · Review & Share Setup [modal flow]
Contains: exact version preview, verified recipient, role, review due date, permissions and optional note.
Actions: preview as guest, grant/request access, copy review link, revoke/withdraw.
States: missing recipient, saving draft, conflicting open request, success/failure.
Never share a working draft by accident.

Document type requirements
Proposal: context, objectives, scope, deliverables, schedule, fee table and assumptions.
Agreement record: parties, scope reference, uploaded/external agreement and acceptance evidence.
Brief: goals, audience, constraints and success criteria.
Welcome pack: next steps, milestones and required inputs.
Notes/deliverable: free body, attachments and handoff.

Explicit later scope
AI generation, template builder, real-time coediting, electronic signing and integrated email sending.
V1 approval is a review decision, not a legal signature.

children.name: Preview status

children.name: Section label
children.characters: PAGE INVENTORY / 5 OF 6 / ALL V1

children.name: Board title
children.characters: A small client experience. Complete owner controls.

children.name: Summary
children.characters: Guest routes expose explicitly granted objects. An invitation never gives workspace-wide access.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
G01 · Invite & Verify [guest flow]
Contains: business identity, masked recipient, project context and access instructions.
Actions: verify identity, enter assigned work.
States: expired/revoked invite, wrong account, resend, unavailable.
Transactional access email only; no general email composer.

G02 · Shared Project [guest page]
Contains: approved shared summary, review requests and delivery packages; requested action/date.
Actions: open assigned review or delivery.
States: no shared work, waiting, complete, revoked.
Exclude private notes, owner tasks and unshared files.

G03 · Review Version [guest page]
Contains: immutable version, brief/context, reviewer, due date, client comments, decision and receipt.
Actions: comment, approve, request changes.
States: pending, submitting, already decided, withdrawn/superseded, unauthorized.
Changes requested requires a comment.
Only the designated reviewer can decide.

G04 · Delivery [guest page]
Contains: package, exact versions/files, handoff notes, sender/date and permitted downloads.
Actions: download, acknowledge receipt.
States: unavailable file, failure, revoked access.
Acknowledgment does not retroactively approve work.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
S01 · Account & Workspace [settings page]
Contains: name/email, password/session controls, workspace name/timezone, notification preferences, Terms/Privacy links.
Actions: update, sign out, request data export/deletion.
States: validation, pending verification, failure.
V1 has one owner; member management comes later.

S02 · Professional Defaults [settings page]
Contains: business/contact details, services, default fee items, document logo/colors and proposal defaults.
Actions: update, preview, restore defaults.
States: unsaved, invalid asset/value, saved.
Defaults apply to new documents; historical versions stay fixed.

S03 · Client Access [settings page]
Contains: recipients, project/document grants, reviewer role, invitation state and last activity.
Actions: invite, resend, revoke, inspect guest preview.
States: pending, active, expired, revoked.
Internal roles and billing controls arrive with their features.

Shared V1 state contract
Every surface covers loading, empty, failure/retry, unauthorized and unavailable record where relevant.
Editing covers dirty/saving/failed save, safe navigation and stale updates.
Destructive actions name affected records; archive offers restore.
Guest work is usable on mobile and keyboard.

children.name: Board title
children.characters: State changes describe what actually happened.

children.name: Summary
children.characters: Lifecycle state, attention flags and access are different dimensions. The following are proposed CoreDesk rules.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
Client / relationship
Prospect → Active → Inactive → Archived
Prospect → Active: first scope acceptance is recorded.
Active → Inactive: no open engagement remains.
Inactive → Active: new engagement starts.
Archive: resolve/move open projects first; preserve history.
Restore: reopens the relationship record, not old projects.

Project / engagement
Draft → Planned → Active → In review
→ Ready to deliver → Delivered → Closed → Archived
Draft: capture client, outcome, scope and owner.
Planned: owner records accepted scope/date/evidence.
Active: work begins.
In review: owner submits required deliverables.
Ready: all required deliverables have approved versions.
Delivered: package sharing or external handoff recorded.
Closed: owner confirms completion.
Archived: read-only history, restorable.

Project exceptions
On hold stores a reason and previous state; Resume returns there.
Cancelled preserves work and closes pending reviews.
Change requests return In review → Active.
Reopen Closed/Delivered → Active creates a new work cycle; prior delivery remains immutable.
Selecting a revised version as required delivery invalidates Ready status until approved. Creating a private draft alone does not.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
Document / content and review
Working draft → Submitted v1 → Approved v1
                         ↘ Changes requested
New draft v2 → Submitted v2 → Approved v2
Approved version → included in Delivery → Archived

Submit freezes version + assets + reviewer + due date.
Comments and outcomes belong to that version/request.
Approval never transfers to a new revision.
A newer draft does not replace the submitted version.
New submission closes/supersedes the prior pending request.
Withdraw closes the request; history remains.
Published older versions are marked Superseded, not erased.

Type-specific distinctions
A proposal decision may inform scope acceptance; the owner records the project transition explicitly.
An agreement record may reference externally accepted terms.
Informational notes need no review until marked as a required deliverable.
Delivered is a package relationship to a version, not proof of signature.

Attention flags / not lifecycle stages
Overdue = due date passed and work incomplete.
Waiting on client = pending client decision/input.
Blocked = explicit blocker and next action.
Show the responsible person, reason and due date.

Archive is not deletion
Archive hides active work and preserves relationships.
Restore does not reactivate expired access grants.
Revoking access remains an explicit action.

children.name: Preview status
children.characters: COREDESK   /   CAPABILITY PREVIEW   /   PROPOSED SCOPE — NOT THE PRINCIPAL PRODUCT DIRECTION

children.name: Section label
children.characters: LIFECYCLES / REVIEW, DELIVERY & ACCESS

children.name: Board title
children.characters: Make decisions and sharing unambiguous.

children.name: Summary
children.characters: V1 supports one workspace owner and one designated approver per review request. Internal team seats are later.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
Review request / one exact version
Owner saves draft → freezes version → picks recipient
→ previews client view → creates request → copies link.
Recipient verifies identity → opens exact version
→ comments → Approves OR Requests changes.
Owner sees outcome → revises OR prepares delivery.
Access email is transactional; manual link sharing is available.

Transition guards
Unsaved/failed-save content cannot be submitted.
One open request per deliverable in V1.
Approving a stale/withdrawn request is rejected.
Repeated submit/decision clicks do not duplicate events.
Reassigning reviewer closes the old request and creates a new one.
Every event records actor, time, version and outcome.

Delivery package
Select approved required versions + immutable supporting file revisions.
Name package, recipient and handoff notes.
Preview contents → share to recipient OR record external handoff.
Record delivered date and method.
Guest downloads; acknowledgment is separate and optional.
Missing approvals or missing files block final delivery.
Changing a package creates a new package revision. Replacing an upload cannot alter a delivered package.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
Owner
Creates/edits all Core records; controls sharing, review requests, delivery, archive and restore.
Internal notes and working drafts are private by default.

Guest reviewer
Reads granted versions and shared project context.
Comments; approves or requests changes only when designated.
Downloads only permitted files.
Cannot see internal notes, search the workspace, edit drafts or invite others.

Guest viewer
Reads/downloads explicitly granted content.
Cannot approve or manage access.

Access lifecycle
Invited → Verified/Active → Expired or Revoked.
Grant includes recipient, object, permissions and expiry.
No inherited access to sibling projects/documents.
Client membership alone grants no content.
Preview must match the real guest experience.

Essential failure paths
Expired invite: request renewed access.
Wrong account: switch identity without revealing content.
Revoked link: clear unavailable state.
Save/export/upload failure: retain input and retry.
Archived object: history view; restore is owner-only.
Activity events are visible only to authorized recipients.

children.characters: PHASED ROADMAP / DEPENDENCY ORDER

children.name: Board title
children.characters: Ship the whole loop before adding more apps.

children.name: Summary
children.characters: Phases are sequenced by dependencies and exit gates. No dates or effort estimates are asserted without team capacity.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
P0 · Product definition / now
Deliver: feature map, IA, page inventory, lifecycle rules, source notes and release boundary.
Exit: review the scope assumptions and validate the journey with target freelancers.
Next design phase begins from these page contracts.

P1 · Core foundation / V1 build
Deliver: identity, recovery, workspace setup; clients/contacts; projects, milestones, tasks; private record access, search, activity and archive.
Depends on: canonical object model and access rules.
Exit: create client/project, find its tasks from any view and restore archived history without duplication.

P2 · Documents / V1 build
Deliver: fixed document types/templates, section editor, save/recovery, version snapshots, preview and PDF export.
Depends on: P1 project context and storage.
Exit: edit, recover a failed save, preview/export and inspect an older immutable version.

P3 · Review to delivery / V1 build
Deliver: guest identity/access, explicit sharing, comments, revision loop, approval, package delivery and acknowledgment.
Depends on: P2 versions + P1 access/activity.
Exit: run the complete owner/client workflow and all access/approval checks.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
P4 · V1 release quality
Deliver: keyboard/mobile guest flow, error recovery, empty states, performance targets, privacy/legal copy and operational support.
Depends on: P1–P3 passing together.
Exit: validation scenarios below pass with test users.
V1 is P1 + P2 + P3 + P4; an internal-only partial build is not the full V1 promise.

P5 · V1.1 / improve repeated work
Prioritize from observed friction: internal team seats, custom templates, import/export, multiple reviewers, connections, reminders and optional AI.
Each extension has separate acceptance criteria.
Do not enable everything at once.

P6 · V2 / optional applications
Portfolio: explicit client consent and selected published material.
Finance: estimates/invoices/payments and reporting.
Choose order from demand; neither blocks V1.
Native e-sign and payment providers require separate integration discovery.

P7 · V3 / Developer discovery
Explore Code, CLI and Agents as a separate workbench.
Define file model, execution permissions, environment and review/recovery before UI.
Do not inherit the discarded Developer screen layout.

children.characters: What must be true before V1 is ready

children.name: Summary
children.characters: These are proposed acceptance targets and design gates, not measured results.

children.name: Left content
children.characters:
1 · First meaningful work
A new owner creates a client, project and first task without guidance in ≤5 minutes.
The same task appears once in project work, global tasks and relevant Home results.

2 · Review and revision integrity
Owner submits v1; client requests changes.
Owner creates and submits v2; client approves v2.
The v1 content, feedback and outcome remain readable.
Opening a version never counts as approval.

3 · Access isolation
Guest A cannot retrieve Client B’s content through navigation, search or direct links.
Private notes and working drafts remain hidden.
Revoked access stops further viewing and actions.

4 · Delivery correctness
A package contains the exact approved versions.
Unapproved required work blocks final delivery.
Download and acknowledgment do not change approval.
Prior package history survives revisions.

5 · Recovery and history
Failed save/export/upload retains recoverable input.
Repeated clicks do not duplicate requests/decisions.
Archive/restore preserves record links and history.
A changed/expired grant does not silently reactivate.

children.name: Right content
children.characters:
Decisions to validate first
Solo-owner V1 plus guest reviewers matches the first audience.
Invite-only client review is worth the V1 scope.
Fixed document types cover the first real projects.
One project owns each task/document.
Portfolio, Finance and Developer can wait.

Next UI sequence / after this planning phase
1. Auth entry + sign in + onboarding.
2. Home + Clients + Client Detail.
3. Project Workspace + task detail.
4. Document editing + preview + history.
5. Guest review + revision + delivery.
6. Settings, archive and system states.
Review each journey before expanding screen count.

Future design criteria
Use retained CoreDesk palette/logo as the starting point.
Client records have consistent fields and clear next action.
Project and document context survives navigation.
Keyboard focus and readable hierarchy are deliberate.
Motion has a purpose and reduced-motion behavior.
Test real long names, empty records and failed actions.

Scope change rule
Record the user problem, affected pages, state/permission impact and release phase before adding a feature.
A new specialist application does not enter V1 by becoming another sidebar item.
